sections.h2: Before you sell fast in Warwick
sections.html:
Warwick has a cost most New York sellers never meet: a town transfer tax that the buyer pays, which shapes how offers are priced. The town is also large, rural in parts and split among several school districts, so where your house sits matters as much as its condition. Know your hamlet, your district and your assessment before talking numbers.

The Town of Warwick fills the southwestern tip of Orange County along the New Jersey line. It spans about 105 square miles and counted 32,027 residents in 2020. Inside it are three incorporated villages (Warwick, Florida and Greenwood Lake) and hamlets that include Amity, Bellvale, Edenville, Pine Island, Sterling Forest and Wisner.

sections.h2: Homes and land across the town
sections.html:
Housing ranges from village streets to lake communities to farmland. Land around Pine Island and Hoopstick sits in the Black Dirt region, known for fertile soil, and Greenwood Lake straddles the New York and New Jersey border. The Appalachian Trail passes through town.

  • Warwick village: centered where NY 94 meets NY 17A.
  • Florida and Greenwood Lake villages: also on NY 17A.
  • Pine Island and the Black Dirt hamlets: farmland and larger lots.
  • Amity, Edenville and New Milford: near the New Jersey line.

Because the lots vary so much, tell buyers exactly what comes with yours: village sewer or septic, lake access, acreage and how far it sits from the village center.

Most of the town lies in the Warwick Valley Central School District. Other parts belong to the Florida Union Free School District, the Greenwood Lake Union Free School District and the Tuxedo Union Free School District. Families usually ask which school their children would attend, so confirm your district before you list instead of guessing from the mailing address.

NY 17A and NY 94 carry most traffic, and Warwick Municipal Airport serves the town. New Jersey Transit buses 196 and 197 run to Manhattan, and a Warwick inter-municipal bus also serves the town.

Warwick charges a transfer tax of three-quarters of one percent on property sales, and the buyer pays it. Voters approved it by referendum in November 2006, and it has applied to conveyances since April 1, 2007, including those inside the villages. The money goes into a fund for open space, farmland, recreation, water resources and historic structures.

The first $100,000 of the price of improved property is exempt, and so is the first $50,000 for unimproved land. The town's own transfer tax form goes to the county clerk with the standard state form, and the deed is not recorded until both are in. Orange County's deed page lists a $5 fee for the Community Preservation Fund form and refers Warwick filers to the town for it.

Because the buyer carries this cost, ask any buyer whether the offer already accounts for it.

The Town Assessor's office in Town Hall, 132 Kings Highway, sets assessments. Warwick's 2026 assessments sit at a uniform level of 7.65 percent of full value as of July 2025, so a low assessed value says nothing about market value. Exemption applications are due March 1 each year, and the office begins taking the next year's applications in July.

An informal review can be requested before the town files its tentative roll on May 1, and the town suggests asking by March 15. Formal complaints go to the Board of Assessment Review on the fourth Tuesday of May.

The Receiver of Taxes collects real property tax from January through March and school tax from September through October. Unpaid taxes go to the Orange County Commissioner of Finance at 255 Main Street in Goshen. Ask for a current bill and a payoff figure before closing.

The Building Department enforces the state and town building codes and issues certificates of occupancy, which the town requires for all building in Warwick. Its office is in Town Hall and is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 4:00. A five-member Zoning Board of Appeals hears requests for relief from the zoning laws. If your house has an open permit or a missing certificate of occupancy, resolve or disclose it before accepting an offer.

Deeds are recorded with the Orange County Clerk. Pay in cash or by check: credit cards are refused, and so are personal checks over $250.

The seller's state deed tax is two dollars per five hundred dollars of price, paid on top of these charges. The Warwick tax above falls on the buyer.

sections.h2: How a Warwick closing fits together
sections.html:
Three separate filings meet at closing, and each goes to a different place. The buyer's attorney or title company sends the deed, the TP-584 and the RP-5217 to the Orange County Clerk, the town's own transfer tax form travels with them, and the Receiver of Taxes provides the payoff for any open town bill.

Start with the town form, since the clerk will not record the deed until both the town and state forms are in. Ask the Town Assessor which exemptions sit on the parcel, and check whether the house is inside a village, because the transfer tax applies there too. Put the answers in writing and hand them to your attorney, who can then close without calling you back for each missing item.

sections.h2: Is a cash offer a good fit?
sections.html:
A cash offer fits when speed or condition matters more than the top price. Houses that struggle with a bank appraisal, such as ones with deferred repairs or an estate that has not settled, are the usual candidates. A cash buyer also works without a lender's timetable.

  • Compare what you would net after the payoff and any tax proration.
  • Ask whether the buyer will close at the Orange County Clerk or through a title company, and who pays for recording.
  • Keep the Warwick transfer tax form on the checklist so the deed is not rejected.

Whichever route you take, gather the deed, the tax bill, permit records and certificate of occupancy before the first showing, so the contract stage is short.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller pay Warwick's transfer tax?
faqs.a: The buyer pays it. Warwick's community preservation tax is three-quarters of one percent of the price, with the first $100,000 of an improved property exempt. The seller still owes the state deed tax of two dollars per five hundred dollars.

faqs.q: Who sets property assessments in the Town of Warwick?
faqs.a: The Town Assessor's office, in Warwick Town Hall at 132 Kings Highway. The 2026 uniform level of assessment is 7.65 percent of full value, so assessed values sit far below market value. Exemption applications are due each March 1.

faqs.q: When are Warwick assessment appeals heard?
faqs.a: The Board of Assessment Review meets on the fourth Tuesday of May. An informal review can be requested earlier, ideally by March 15, before the tentative roll is filed on May 1.

faqs.q: Which office records the deed on a Warwick sale?
faqs.a: The Orange County Clerk. The fee list shows $45 flat, $5 per page, $5 for the TP-584 and $125 for the RP-5217 on a single family house, payable by cash or check. Personal checks over $250 are refused.

faqs.q: Which school district covers my Warwick house?
faqs.a: Most of the town is in the Warwick Valley Central School District. Other parts fall in the Florida, Greenwood Lake or Tuxedo Union Free School Districts, so check the district for your exact parcel before you list.
